Apple beats on quarterly revenue in CEO John Ternus’ first earnings report

Apple reported better-than-expected revenue but came up short of estimates on iPad sales for the fiscal fourth quarter.
Here’s how the company did compared to analysts’ estimates, according to LSEG.
EPS: $2.10.
Revenue: $114.48 billion vs. $113.39 billion expected
It’s Apple’s first earnings report since CEO John Ternus took the helm on Sept. 1, succeeding Tim Cook. CNBC isn’t immediately comparing the earnings figure to LSEG’s estimate of $1.99 per share.
Revenue increased 12% from $102.5 billion a year earlier, Apple said in a statement on Monday. The company reported iPhone revenue of $57.58 billion, topping estimates of $56.54 billion, according to LSEG.
Apple’s iPhone revenue in the quarter only included eight days of new Phone 18 Pro sales. And Apple’s new flagship device, the iPhone Duo, didn’t hit store shelves until the period was over.
During the quarter, Apple raised prices on iPhones by $100, reflecting a worldwide shortage on memory and other components.
Monday’s earnings call, set to start at 5 p.m. ET, will be the first with Ternus at the helm. Investors want to hear from him about the company’s plans in China after its AI software got approved, as well as the slew of recent product launches and how the company continues to grapple with global shortages of memory and flash storage.
Apple’s iPad division contracted over 10% on an annual basis during the quarter to $6.22 billion in sales. It was the worst performing of all of Apple’s product categories by growth.
The company released a new iPad Mini last month, and updated the iPad Air back in March, but the product line has not had many significant updates this year. Apple’s iPad division declined 6% year-over-year during the June quarter, too.
Ternus blamed supply constraints and a difficult comparison to last year as reasons for the iPad’s performance.
Gross margin in focus due to high component prices:
Apple’s gross margin is being closely watched as the company is being battered by higher prices for key components, such as storage, memory, and chips.
The gross margin was 47.9%, including a favorable impact of approximately 1 percentage point from tariff refunds. It’s a major drop from last quarter’s 50.1% gross margin.
It’s unclear if analysts factored any potential tariff refund impact in their projections. Had they not, gross margin would have been short of the 47.5% consensus estimate from LSEG.

Brazilian stock market probably overreacted to election results

This month in international markets saw significant volatility in Brazilian equities. EWZ, which tracks the MSCI Brazil GRTR USD index, surged +12.5% at the beginning of the month, as it priced in the probability of a Flavio Bolsonaro win after a strong showing in round one of the Brazilian elections. However, when the dust had settled, Lula unexpectedly came from behind, and the EWZ gave back all its gains and then some, with a -18.4% drop on Monday.
I wanted to figure out the investors viewed Bolsonaro as so much more market friendly. Curiously, I found that the Brazilian stock market did extremely well during Lula's two prior terms and the third current term and was slightly negative during the presidency of Jair Bolsonaro, the father of losing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro. In Brazil, the presidential terms are four years long and align neatly with the calendar year. This makes it really easy to track returns using the MSCI Brazil, which would be the gold standard anyway. All returns are gross returns using USD currency:
Term Start End Total Return CAGR Lula 1 2003 2006 +571.85% +61.10% Lula 2 2007 2010 +93.14% +17.86% Bolsonaro 2019 2022 (-2.47%) (-0.62%) Lula 3 2023 10/27/26 +56.63% +12.45% Lula, Total -- -- +1932.44% +29.01%
I certainly would not have expected the less market friendly candidate to outperform his counterpart (presumably with similar policies as his son) by such a drastic margin, even after eating that monster -18.4% single day drop this week. However, to be fair, Lula 1 was an incredible time for emerging markets, one which likely could not be reproduced again. And Bolsonaro's presidency coincided with the pandemic, which could have hampered returns.
To control for this, I compared the MSCI Brazil against several other benchmarks to which the country belongs. ACWI includes all countries, ACWI ex-USA is the international market excluding the USA, and emerging markets are the MSCI emerging markets. Additionally, while Brazil does not belong to the MSCI USA, MSCI World (a misnomer which means developed markets including USA), and MSCI World ex-USA (developed markets excluding USA), these are included for comparison. Brazil has trounced all of these benchmarks under Lula's presidency and badly lagged all of them under Jair Bolsonaro.

Palantir raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales top US government revenue for the first time

Palantir (PLTR) beat Wall Street estimates on its third quarter revenue and profit on Monday and raised its full-year revenue outlook as the data software company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever.
Palantir reported Q3 revenue of $2.313 billion, a 96% increase from the previous year. Wall Street had expected revenue of $2.17 billion, according to Bloomberg data.
Palantir now sees full-year revenue between $8.530 billion and $8.534 billion, topping analyst estimates of $8.2 billion. The company also raised its US commercial sales target to more than $3.559 billion. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 also beat consensus estimates of $0.40.

The attention economy is a relic of the 2010s and $META is a $1 trillion boomer casino with a GPU addiction

Zuck is about to spend the GDP of a developing nation trying to solve a problem his company is financially incentivized to never solve.
The entire premise of AI is that you can accomplish shit faster. Research something in 10 seconds. Find what you need. Automate tedious tasks. Close the app and go touch grass.
Meta's entire business model is making sure you do absolutely none of those things.
Exhibit A: Instagram. Want to listen to a video with your screen off? Nice try buddy. Get those eyeballs back on the screen, daddy Zuck has ad impressions to serve.
Exhibit B: Facebook Marketplace. This company employs some of the smartest engineers on earth and somehow searching for a $200 table within 15 miles returns a jet ski in Delaware, three Temu dropshippers and a 2006 Nissan Altima with no title. You think this is an accident? I refuse to believe the company building frontier AI cannot implement a few simple filters.
Exhibit C: Facebook itself. An industrial-scale retirement home dopamine dispenser. Your uncle is on hour four of watching AI-generated murder documentaries narrated by a British robot while arguing with a fake veteran about immigration. The algorithm has determined his remaining cognitive capacity is worth approximately $0.17 CPM.
And now Zuck is proposing to “save” people time with his new shopping bot and little AI tool. Sure, users will then have more time to watch reels subtly embedded with more targeted ads. But do people really think Meta is incentivized to help you order a fucking watermelon from Instacart more efficiently?
Here is the actual investment thesis:
AI theoretically eliminates the middleman between wanting something and getting it.
Unfortunately Meta IS the fucking middleman.
If AI makes shopping, searching, and consuming information dramatically faster, plus unbundles how creators find consumers, what happens to a business that makes money when those activities take longer?
You have a trillion-dollar company spending astronomical amounts on compute to build technology that, if it actually works in the consumer's interest, undermines the engagement economics of its own products.
It's like Marlboro spending $100 billion developing a cure for nicotine addiction and then trying to monetize the cure with cigarette ads.
TLDR: Meta is trying to invent the future while its entire business model is trapping divorced dads in a 2014 BuzzFeed slideshow. AI compresses time, Meta sells time. Muse is going to end up having a quicker death than the Metaverse.

Oracle jumped 11% after putting a date on positive free cash flow. It's still 56% below its record

Oracle closed at $144.54 on Wednesday, up 10.7%, after its investor day put a date on the cash turn: free cash flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 (December 2027 to May 2028), then $30B+ in fiscal 2029. Last fiscal year it was -$23.7B.
The interesting part is how it gets there. Capex still peaks over the next two years. What changes is who pays upfront: customer prepayments, customer-supplied hardware, and a $20B cap on new capital-markets money through fiscal 2030, after $20B of stock sold this summer.
Even after Wednesday, it closed 56% below its September 2025 record. The date is new. The spending isn't.

Samsung Electronics Forecasts $420 Billion Operating Profit in 2027 Despite Stock Slump. HBM Prices to Rise 100–150%

According to an analysis by KB Securities, Samsung Electronics has secured long term supply contracts for approximately 80 percent of its scheduled 2027 memory semiconductor production, positioning the company for potential earnings growth despite recent stock price declines.
KB Securities research head Kim Dong won detailed that Samsung finalized five year agreements covering 70 percent of its general purpose DRAM and NAND flash memory production with major global tech firms, while securing long term contracts for its entire annual high bandwidth memory production volume.
The company expects strong financial performance driven by rising prices and a product mix shift toward HBM4, which is projected to account for 80 percent of Samsung's HBM sales next year and offers a 40 percent power efficiency improvement over HBM3E.
Consequently, average HBM selling prices are anticipated to jump 100 to 150 percent next year, pushing first quarter DRAM prices up by double digits and raising projected operating profit to 367 trillion Korean won this year and 555 trillion Korean won next year. While Samsung's stock price dropped 19 percent recently due to broader macroeconomic uncertainties and concerns over artificial intelligence investment sustainability, KB Securities views the drop as a valuation adjustment rather than a decline in the company's core profit generating capabilities.

US inflation rises more than expected ahead of midterm elections

US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.
The pace of price rises increased to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August.
Inflation was above forecasts, driven by higher gasoline prices which have spiked following disruption to Middle East energy supplies due to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.
The elections are being fought over cost of living pressures across the US.
Source: BBC

Samsung forecasts record third-quarter profit of $80 billion for the first time in history - Operating profit jumped 782%

Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported third-quarter preliminary operating profit of 107.40 trillion won ($80.2 billion), surging past 100 trillion won for the first time in the company’s history as booming demand for artificial intelligence continues to fuel its chips business.
Quarterly operating profit jumped 782% from a year earlier. Revenue came in at about 195 trillion won, up nearly 127% from the same period last year.
Samsung, the world’s largest memory chipmaker, has benefited from surging demand for memory used in AI infrastructure. In the second quarter, the company posted record revenue of 171.5 trillion won and record operating profit of 89.5 trillion won, driven by its memory business.
The company has also stepped up investments and partnerships tied to AI. In September, Samsung announced a strategic partnership with French artificial intelligence startup Mistral AI, with plans to deploy the startup’s AI models across its semiconductor operations.

GOOGL: Everyone Was Bullish Yesterday, Now Google Is Suddenly Dead?

It’s crazy how sentiment on X and investing forums flipped overnight. Yesterday, everyone was praising Google’s AI potential and growth. Today, people are acting like the entire business is falling apart. Just search the ticker on X and people are bring out 5 year bearish outlooks for Google, one of the best companies on earth with one of the best margins and healthy track records.
Alphabet reported 25% revenue growth to $127.6B, 30% operating income growth, and 103% growth in Google Cloud. Search is in fact still growing (although not like before), Gemini is expanding, and the company maintains a massive ecosystem with healthy operating margins. Yes, AI spending, competition, and regulation are legitimate risks, but the underlying business is still growing. No one is mentioning growth of cloud and how it’s on track of surpassing search by 29-30. People who think Google is an ad play they need to understand TPUs and how they revolutionized GCP.
Historically, major MAG7 companies have weathered serious sell-offs and recovered over longer time frames. There is no guarantee every company will recover from every decline, but these businesses have demonstrated remarkable resilience through strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and substantial cash generation.
Some people talk about Google as if it’s a heavily indebted company struggling to survive, like a business burdened by expensive debt. Alphabet has a very different financial profile, with substantial cash reserves, strong operating profits, and the ability to fund its investments at scale.
And lastly remember folks who were bearish $MSFT when it was $360 few months ago!! I am getting similar vibes. I remain super bullish into 27-28 and expect we reach new all time highs within the next 2 years.

In Q4 2019 Google search was 60% of Google’s revenue and today it’s under 50%. Google has become a very diversified business

Too many financial commentators, analysts and algo traders are focusing too much on the potential decline of search and advertising revenue and are missing the forest for the trees.
In 2019 Google search revenue was $27B and total revenues were $46B, meaning search accounted for just shy of 60% of google’s entire revenue. If we take a look at ad revenues as a whole at the time it would be 82% of all revenues.
Today search has grown from $27B -> $63B, but as percent of total revenues it is now under 50% ($63B out of $127B). Furthermore advertising revenue in aggregate has gone from 82% of quarterly revenue to just 64%. Google has become a more diversified and resilient business and I don’t think this is being appreciated enough.
Let’s say search revenue flat lines or worse case declines and 5 years from now it drops from $63B -> $45B a quarter. If all of google’s other revenue sources continue to grow, i wouldn’t be surprised if search at that point would only be 30% of google’s entire revenue and they are doing $150B a quarter
$60B GCP
$20B YT
$20B subscriptions
$4B network ads (assuming this declines as well)
$1B other bets (waymo ramping up)
Will all the pundits still be upset at a flatlining or declining search revenue then? I don’t think so

Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks

Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as “the front page of the internet.”
The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company’s shares dropped over 11% after its numbers were released.
Here’s how the company did compared with LSEG estimates:
Earnings per share: $1.40 vs. $1.35 expected
Revenue: $895 million vs. $878 million expected
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company’s shrinking search-referral traffic from Google played a major role in its planned efforts to require people to become “logged-in” users.
A previous Google search update designed to surface “authentic” content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant’s continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic.
Huffman didn’t provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity. The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.
He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.
Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.

Amazon misses on earnings and holds capex steady, adding to AI spending jitters

Here’s how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:
Earnings per share: $1.89 vs. $1.96 estimated
Revenue: $201.94 billion vs. $202.31 billion estimated
Wall Street was also looking at other key revenue numbers:
Amazon Web Services: $45.98 billion vs. $45.29 billion, according to StreetAccount
Advertising: $19.64 billion vs. $20.82 billion, according to StreetAccount
The company held steady on its capital expenditure forecast for 2026, saying it continues to expect spending will reach $220 billion this year.
Tech’s hyperscalers have been on a blistering spending run to meet the surge in demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, but signs have begun to emerge that the capex splurge is moderating. Earlier this week, Microsoft lowered its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, while Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.
Amazon posted negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, recording an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve month period, an increase of 386% year over year. In the prior quarter, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion.
